label: early copy steps (2nd/3rd output) of long sequences, when input is w/a/0/u/m/g/k/t/b
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely on the steps that output the 2nd or 3rd original token (recall_idx 1-2, i.e. the 1st and 2nd steps after <DEL>; 98% of mass). It never fires in the original phase or on the <DEL> step itself. Firing rate and magnitude go up with sequence length: L=9 holds 74% of the mass, L=8 21%, and it is essentially silent for L<=5. recall_idx 1 (input = first original token) is stronger than recall_idx 2. On top of that it depends on the current input token: w is by far the strongest (the top examples are all w as the first token, input right after <DEL>), followed by a, 0, u, m, then g, k, t, b. q, i and o are weak. The behaviour is graded, a soft product of length and token identity, so a boolean predicate misses low-amplitude firings on other tokens and on L=7, and many predicted steps stay below threshold. Coarser window (recall_idx 1-2 only): recall 0.97 but precision 0.06.
